items.title: Manuel Mello Interview, 1959-08-03
items.q: So everybody with the exception of Schilling and Philly Marsloff... We formed a brass band and the brass band stuck, oh I guess in about 1909.

ctx.x: They did have, Steckler, Steckler's band went out of, uh, they, they, they, they, they,

they disbanded. And, and, and, and the, uh, Spanish-American war why one or two of the fellow signed up and went to the army and the band, why just disbanded and they was never reorganized. So let's see, they had another band. I believe that was O'Ramus' band. That was three pieces. Guitar, bass, and violin.

The You're talking about Ramis' band? Or Amis. Or Amis. That's the only other string band that I knew of at that particular time that was playing. And it's going around a three-piece job, not a whole lot of... Just, they never played a whole lot of big music. They played three pieces bass, violin, guitar. And what would they play like? Would they play by music? No, no, by hand.
